metadata.title: Why Your AI File Got Marked When No Law Said It Had To.
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: which law made my file carry a mark? Lands the carry-out that a global setting is a company's choice, not a mandate.
metadata.factcheck: FACTCHECK.md — legal claims from supplied research, NOT first-party. Verify before PUBLISH (not before render).
metadata.anchor_pair: S03 -> S13 (must be the SAME composition)
metadata.one_flag: S12 — the cheap-pipeline explanation, flagged as undocumented
metadata.recurring: S06 -> S07 -> S14 reuse the same two rule-shapes

beats.narration_text: Someone asked which law made their AI images carry a hidden mark. Turns out, probably none of them. Liam. Take them through it.

shot.new_visual_element: Shannon puppet, lab, speaks to camera, hands off

beats.note: Audio baked into media/B00.mp4 by Seedance (voice MARCUS). No mp3 for this beat.

beats.narration_text: If you're not in the EU or California, there is a good chance no law required the mark on your file.

shot.new_visual_element: A marked file; an empty rule-slot

production_viz.label: A marked file; an empty rule-slot
production_viz.mechanic: A single file on cream carrying a small terracotta mark. Beside it, an outlined empty slot labelled for a rule — nothing fills it.

beats.narration_text: It's there anyway, and that difference matters more than it sounds.

production_viz.label: Held: mark present, rule absent
production_viz.mechanic: The mark and the empty slot held together, unchanged. Nothing resolves.

beats.narration_text: Hold on to one session: you generate an image and an essay, same tool, same afternoon.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — one image, one essay

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — one image, one essay
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Two files side by side on cream — a picture and a page of text — same timestamp beneath both. THIS EXACT COMPOSITION RETURNS AT S13.

beats.narration_text: The usual explanation is that Europe passed a rule and everyone worldwide had to follow.

production_viz.label: The Brussels-effect reading
production_viz.mechanic: One rule-shape at the centre radiating outward across a globe, covering everything. Sell the Brussels-effect reading as reasonable.

beats.narration_text: But the European rule bites when a system is sold into Europe or its output is used there — not on every file made everywhere.

shot.new_visual_element: The rule contracts to its nexus

production_viz.label: The rule contracts to its nexus
production_viz.mechanic: The radiating coverage contracts sharply back to a bounded EU-nexus region. Most of the globe is left uncovered.

beats.narration_text: And here's the giveaway: Europe's rule covers synthetic text, and California's marking duty doesn't.

production_viz.label: One covers text, one doesn't
production_viz.mechanic: Two rule-shapes side by side. Under each, the media it covers. One includes a text block; the other visibly omits it.

beats.narration_text: If a single mandate were driving all this, the rules wouldn't disagree about what to mark.

production_viz.label: Out of register
production_viz.mechanic: The two rule-shapes held and overlaid — they fail to register. The misalignment is the whole image.

beats.narration_text: What actually exists is a patchwork.

production_viz.label: A patchwork, not a rule
production_viz.mechanic: Several separate rule-shapes on cream, distinct, none merging into a single form.

beats.narration_text: Different laws, landing on different people, covering different content, starting on different dates.

shot.new_visual_element: Four columns, no two rows alike

production_viz.label: Four columns, no two rows alike
production_viz.mechanic: Four columns fill in sequence with the narration: WHO / WHAT / WHEN / WHERE. Every row differs from every other.

beats.narration_text: Some land on the company that made the file, some on the platform that hosts it, some only on advertisers.

production_viz.label: One file, three duty-points
production_viz.mechanic: One file travelling left to right past three parties — maker, host, advertiser — each with a different duty attaching at its own point.

beats.narration_text: And in the United States there's no general federal rule at all — the one that got closest was revoked, and the bills that would have replaced it didn't pass.

production_viz.label: The federal slot, empty
production_viz.mechanic: A slot labelled for a federal rule, drawn empty. Beside it, two faded shapes: one struck through, one never completed.

beats.narration_text: One flag — the obvious next question is why mark everything anyway, and the usual answer, that one pipeline is cheaper than sorting users by location, is a reasonable guess nobody has actually documented.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ONE FLAG — a reasonable guess

production_viz.label: THE ONE FLAG — a reasonable guess
production_viz.mechanic: The cheap-pipeline explanation rendered inside a dotted border, captioned 'reasonable, undocumented'. A single terracotta FLAG marker over the beat — the reel's only hedge, labelled as one.

beats.narration_text: Which brings back your session: the image carried a mark, the essay probably didn't, and that split follows the rules, not the tool.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — one marked, one bare

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — one marked, one bare
production_viz.mechanic: THE S03 COMPOSITION RETURNS, identical — same two files, same timestamp. Only change: a terracotta mark sits on the image; the essay stays bare.

beats.narration_text: Two files, one company, one afternoon, and different answers — because the rules were never one rule.

production_viz.label: Two files, two rules
production_viz.mechanic: The two files held. Two separate rule-shapes descend, each pointing at a different file. They never merge.

beats.narration_text: So a mark on your file doesn't prove a law required it — it may just be how the product is built.

production_viz.label: Marked, and no law proven
production_viz.mechanic: MARK PRESENT at the top; an arrow to the conclusion 'A LAW REQUIRED THIS' — struck through terracotta.

beats.narration_text: And no mark doesn't mean no rule applies — some duties land on the platform that hosts the file, long after you've made it.

production_viz.label: Unmarked, and still covered
production_viz.mechanic: Mirroring S15: NO MARK at the top; an arrow to 'NO RULE APPLIES' — struck through. A duty attaches downstream, after the file leaves.

beats.narration_text: Nobody passed a law requiring this everywhere. A global setting is a company's choice, not a government's order.

props.quote: Nobody passed a law requiring this everywhere. A global setting is a company's choice, not a government's order.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Pick one thing your tools do automatically that you assume a law requires: a cookie banner, a data-retention window, an age gate, a disclosure line. Find the actual rule, then check who it binds, what it covers, and where it applies. Note every place the product does more than the rule asks. That gap is almost always somebody's choice — and choices can be argued with. Liam, in for Bear.
